title: Ravensgate invoice and surcharge engine

act2.summary: compliance flags low-value invoices for review - a new notification threshold, unaffected by line construction or surcharges

solutions.title: One shared function decides who hears about an invoice
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that which channels get notified was the pressure most likely to grow a new threshold, and pulled it into one function shared by both entry points. The low-value-review rule arrives on exactly that axis: one new clause, in the one place notification is decided, at 4 lines across 2 hunks.

solutions.title: One shared function decides what an order line becomes on the invoice
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that how a line is built, by kind, was the pressure worth relieving first - a reasonable bet, since a new bundle rule or a new line kind is exactly the sort of thing product would ask for. The low-value-review rule never touches line construction at all: notification routing was never pulled out, so it still duplicates the new clause across both entry points, at exactly the no-pattern baseline's cost.

reviewFocus: Does the reader's own restructuring name, honestly, which pressure it chose to relieve - line construction, or notification - and admit the other is still duplicated?
Would a reader who restructured line-construction instead of notification-routing still recognize, from the measured numbers alone, why the low-value-review rule landed cheaply or expensively?
Does the WALKTHROUGH.md for the losing route say plainly that its bet didn't pay off for this act 2, without pretending its own restructuring was worthless in general?
Do both routes agree, byte for byte, with src/ on every act-1 outcome before the low-value-review rule exists?

For a kata that ships without tests: does the reader's own safety net actually exercise all three cross-cutting concerns - line kinds, surcharge stacking, and the notification threshold - or only the happy path?
